original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/audit_mixed_point.py:scalar_check emit the same circuit_sha256 digest lines (and the same support/topology rejection checks) without per-node json.dumps, so the historical mixed-point and early-sharing scalar streams keep fieldwise-identical receipts?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering (seed 1e60c388106de197fb515e8dc9b5a10f) after the complex-mechanisms draw landed on saturated packing/rank-shape work listed as deferred. Profiling named scalar_check's per-node json.dumps stream inside audit_mixed_point / audit_early_sharing as the bottleneck on this fixed historical screen.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: mixed-point and early-sharing certificates are part of verify-certificates. A faster identical scalar digest does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving scalar_check digest change with frozen baseline, identical mixed-point and early-sharing mathematical payloads, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Do not reopen the mathematical screens or run the selected cold frontier replay.
evidence: PASS_MIXED_POINT_SCALAR_DIGEST via research/mixed-point-scalar-digest/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_MIXED_POINT_SCALAR_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; mixed-point and early-sharing certificate mathematical payloads match the committed files (audit_mixed_point.py is not a source_sha256 pin in either certificate).
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Can the same byte-identical hand-rolled digest pattern accelerate SharedPointCircuit.verify / ExclusionCircuit.verify without changing circuit_sha256?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those verifiers still call json.dumps once per active node on large common-point circuits.
open_questions.first_step: Profile SharedPointCircuit.verify for the h=50 bit-compression local circuit and compare a hand-rolled line writer against the committed digest.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of this session's stop rule; scalar_check was the profiled mixed-point bottleneck.

open_questions.question: Should certificates/mixed-point-audit.json refresh its stale rational_span_frames.py source_sha256 pin (live digest already differs on main)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pin is historical provenance for an unchanged mathematical payload; leaving it avoids mixing a tooling PR with an unrelated pin repair.
open_questions.first_step: Open a dedicated provenance follow-up that only rewrites the three source_sha256 entries after a clean certificate regenerate.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pin repair is outside this tooling change.
